entries.name: Amara
entries.summary: Gives older adults a voice-controlled tablet for family calls, music, and reminders.

scene.job: It gives an older adult a voice-controlled tablet for calls, music, and reminders, while the family manages it from an app.
scene.seller: Adult children and other family members buy the membership.
scene.payer: The family pays privately.

deep_dive.product: Amara Home is a voice-operated tablet that arrives pre-configured. Older adults speak to call family, play radio, hear reminders, and ask questions. Relatives manage setup via a family app. Company page: DSGVO on European servers; membership includes tablet, dock, family app, and content.
deep_dive.how_it_works: 1) Device ships set up. 2) User speaks. 3) Family uses the app for photos, messages, calendar. WLAN or integrated SIM; no smartphone required for the older adult.
deep_dive.user: Older adults living at home (company framing: Oma / Opa).
deep_dive.payer: Private pay / family membership. No SGB XI or DiPA listing found on company page.
deep_dive.business_model: Membership bundling hardware and content. Exact euro list price on the public homepage fetch: not found.
deep_dive.traction: AgeTechX Ones to Watch 2026. Customer quotes dated 2026 on site. Public install counts: not found.
deep_dive.funding: EUR 3.7 million pre-seed; investors Econa, Caesar VC, IBB Ventures (IBB Ventures news). Legal entity H2 Technologies GmbH, founded 2025 by Philipp Hartz and Richard Hector; team about eight (same source).
deep_dive.team: Co-founders Philipp Hartz and Richard Hector (company site; IBB Ventures; AgeTechX speaker page for Hector).
deep_dive.competitors: Senior tablets and senior apps (company table). In our scan: Harmonica/Olympia, inTouch, Zenaris.
deep_dive.regulatory: Consumer / private device. No DiGA or DiPA listing found. Company claims DSGVO / EU servers.
deep_dive.thesis: Interpreted: serves aging adults who will not use a normal tablet; job is connection and light daily structure; seller Amara to the family; payer is the family. Why now: loneliness products sell on affection; DE survey context in T07 shows loneliness is not simply highest at 76+. Kill risk: T07 is kill on the pickable menu; no Kasse path found; crowded check-in shelf.
risks: No named DE payer beyond family cash.
T07 theme is kill on the pickable menu.
Hardware CapEx and churn not published.
deep_dive.relevance: Tied to T07 (social isolation). Standing disposition: kill. Cards T07-H1 and T07-H2 are stressed, still standing as what-ifs, not build permission.
open_questions: Who cancels: older adult or family?
